title: Fast split-aware discriminant prefactorization
objective: Accelerate exact split-aware polynomial prefactorization of large discriminant components with a source-transparent packed kernel, preserving the ordinary-Python oracle, fail-closed fallback, corruption rejection, and degree-90 performance evidence

handoff.summary: Adds an ordinary-Python, source-transparent packed composite polynomial gcd traversal and selects it only for compiled high-workload discriminant prefactorization. The host validates every exported divisor and falls back to the readable oracle on unavailable compilation, overflow, malformed status, or corrupt output. CPython, generated-dynamic, and compiled differentials cover split, no-split, unresolved, invalid-storage, and corruption outcomes. The degree-90 receipt records exact component equality, certificate replay, a 3.94x isolated gcd speedup, and a 2.04x full decomposition speedup (6.582s to 3.224s).
risks: The new mathematical source raises the number-field-algorithms lazy package from below its 1,000,000-byte budget to 1,002,539 bytes; architecture:check reaches and passes FFI lowering, then fails this existing central manifest budget. Integration must make an explicit package-budget decision.

A temporary docstring-only source fingerprint experiment after the validated dd2fdd85 checkpoint caused the native registry to select dynamic execution; it was fully reverted. The earlier passing compiled differential and benchmark both bind to dd2fdd85.
The remaining 3.224-second degree-90 decomposition tail is not closed and still contains repeated perfect-power and probable-primality classification work.
next_steps: Register packed_composite_polynomial_split_hint_in_place in the shared production native-kernel registry and add the focused test to shared manifests.
Add discriminant_prefactor_kernel.py to the shared strict-Python configuration if the integration branch uses explicit module enumeration.
Resolve the 2,539-byte number-field-algorithms lazy-budget overage explicitly, then rerun architecture:check and the production native suite.
Profile the compiled residual using counters before selecting the next theorem-backed perfect-power or primality boundary.
